question.leadin: Give the following about the history of Mexico.
question.text: At its height, this center of the Aztec empire has been estimated to be one of the largest cities in the world. Mexico City was built on its ruins.
question.clue: A large massacre during a religious ceremony was ordered by Pedro de Alvarado near this city's Templo Mayor Complex.

swap.leadin: This empire engaged in ritualized "flower wars" with its neighbors.
swap.text: Identify this Mesoamerican empire whose capital was Tenochtitlan. They were defeated by Hernan Cortez.
swap.clue: Though not the origin of the process, this empire's language is the origin of the word nixtamalization ("NISH-tuh-muhl-uh-zay-shun"), which was typically carried out by the women of this empire.

question.leadin: This archeological site contains a temple called El Castillo, dedicated to the god Kukulcan, which has 365 steps representative of the number of days in the year.
question.text: Name this archeological site in the Yucatan peninsula, which was excavated by the American archaeologist Edward Herbert Thompson. The first chacmool, a statue depicting a reclining figure, was discovered at this site.
question.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

swap.text: This civilization, that was centered on the Yucatan peninsula, created a calendar that predicted the end of the world to be on December 21, 2012, and built the city of Chichen Itza.
swap.clue: Guatemala committed a genocide against this civilization, whose howler monkey gods were chronicled in the Popul Vuh.

question.text: Under the direction of Enrico Martinez, the Spanish conquerors of Tenochtitlan drained this body of water upon which the city was built.

swap.leadin: Before the Aztecs, the Zapotecs lived in the present-day Mexican state of Oaxaca.
swap.text: The Zapotecs adopted this sport from the Olmecs. This sport was played with a solid rubber object, and the Aztecs may have used it to defuse conflicts and resolve disputes.
swap.clue: Participants in this activity attached thin stone heads resembling ax blades to heavy belts known as yokes.

question.leadin: This man's coronation is documented on the Stone of the Five Suns.
question.text: Name this Aztec Emperor, whose possible death by stoning during La Noche Triste ended his captivity under Hernan Cortes.
question.clue: Shortly after this man's death, his people assassinated the rearguard of an invading force in the Night of Sorrows massacre.

swap.leadin: This man fathered the first mestizo child with an interpreter usually known as La Malinche.
swap.text: Name this Spanish conquistador who invaded and conquered the Aztec Empire. Early in his campaign, this man scuttled his ships so that his soldiers would fight without thought of retreat.
swap.clue: This man won the Battle of Otumba and fathered a child with his translator, La Malinche.

question.text: Seventh century CE rulers of this city adopted the title of "ball player" when they took the throne of this Maya city in modern-day Chiapas.
question.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

swap.text: Some of the best-preserved ball courts are at this Mayan site in modern-day Guatemala. It contains the Lost World complex and the Temple of the Great Jaguar.
swap.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

question.leadin: NASA archaeologist Tom Sever pioneered the use of remote sensing to study this civilization's collapse.
question.text: Name this Mesoamerican civilization whose decline in the 8th and 9th centuries led to the effective abandonment of cities like Tikal in the Yucatan peninsula.
question.clue: The Temple of Inscriptions houses anajaw("ah-how")from this civilizationknown as Pacal the Great who reigned for 68 years in its city-state of Palenque("pah-LEN-kay").

swap.leadin: Identify these pre-Columbian civilizations of the Americas.
swap.text: This civilization founded a number of city-states in the Yucutan Peninsula, including Tikal and Chichen Itza.
swap.clue: Pakal was one ruler of this civilization, which used cenotes (suh-no-tays) for the worship of their rain god.

question.text: This culture used the Isthmian script to produce an early form of the Long Count calendar with a fixed beginning. This culture, named for coming after its predecessor, continued using its predecessor's capital at Tres Zapotes.
question.answerHtml: Epi-Olmec culture [do not accept or prompt on Olmecs]

swap.leadin: Archaeologists often point to this Mesoamerican civilization as a "mother culture."
swap.text: Name this civilization whose major archaeological sites include San Lorenzo and La Venta. Jade facsimiles of their iconic colossal heads were found amongst the Mayans.
swap.clue: This Mesoamerican civilization was the first to practice ritual bloodletting and play the ball game, according to artifacts found near their cities like San Lorenzo and La Venta.

question.text: Even earlier than in India, the Mayans used a seashell to represent zero on this calendar system, which divides time into units such as baktun and katun.

swap.text: After the decline of San Lorenzo, the center of the Olmec culture shifted to this city, which became its second capital.
swap.clue: This Olmec site became important due to its abundant rainfall, which eliminated the need for an extensive irrigation system. It was located in modern-day Tabasco, and its Great Pyramid, due to erosion, is conical in shape.

question.leadin: This suburban community, originally known as "Squattersville," inspired Curtis White's novel The Idea of Home.
question.text: Name this Bay Area "village," one of the first preplanned communities in the U.S., whose houses for returning World War II servicemen were mass-produced by the David D. Bohannon Company using the "California method."
question.clue: This city was the original center of Olmec civilization, before it was supplanted by La Venta and Tres Zapotes.

swap.text: An early New Philology work was Sarah Cline's thesis on Culhuacan, which may have been the first town that planted crops on these "floating islands" in the Valley of Mexico.
swap.clue: The name of these places translates to "square made of canes place", reflecting their construction using zoquimatl with wattle.

question.leadin: FTPE answer some questions about a historical city.
question.text: It contains great plazas, truncated pyramids, a court for playing the ball game tlachtli, underground passageways, and about 170 tombs. The Temple of the Danzantes which holds hundreds of conquest slabs is probably its most famous building.
question.clue: Another monument depicts men with scrolls in place of their genitalia who likely represent mutilated war captives - that being the Temple of the Danzantes, or the "Building of the Dancers."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about "Dual-Processual Theory" of Mesoamerican archaeology.
swap.text: The theory uses thiscihuacoatl's[kih-wuh-KWAH-tull] centering of Aztec ideology on the Flower Wars to exemplify both strategies. This general organized his uncle Itzcoatl [its-KWAH-tull] I's book-burnings to wipe out knowledge of prior history.
swap.clue: This Mesoamerican political leader who served as the first cihuacoatl ("see-wa-CO-aht"), or "female serpent", an office which served as the chief deputy of the Aztec emperor.
